claims.text: Random HfNbTaTiZr is a chemically disordered solid solution.
Random HfNbTaTiZr has significant force-constant fluctuations and broadened phonon linewidths because of mass and atomic-size mismatch.
Thermal annealing or controlled cooling can induce HfTi and TiZr short-range-order clusters in HfNbTaTiZr.
HfTi and TiZr short-range-order clusters can percolate and evolve into ordered B2-like superstructures.
The treatment temperature must activate atomic diffusion while remaining below the bulk melting point.
Maintaining a single-phase BCC or FCC matrix avoids scattering from secondary precipitates.
Ordered B2-like binary clusters reduce local lattice strain relative to the random HfNbTaTiZr environment.
Ordered B2-like binary clusters reduce the variance of local atomic force constants.
Reduced force-constant variance and lattice distortion suppress high-frequency phonon scattering and narrow phonon linewidths.
Ordering changes the high-frequency phonon DOS from a broadened, glass-like distribution toward a sharper, Debye-like profile.
Percolating low-distortion ordered clusters create high-conductivity pathways that overcome scattering in the residual disordered matrix.
Percolative B2-like ordering increases the lattice thermal conductivity of HfNbTaTiZr relative to its random state.
FeCoCrMnNi exhibits phonon linewidth broadening or attenuation relative to simple monatomic elements.
Force-constant fluctuations drive phonon attenuation in FeCoCrMnNi.
Random HfNbTaTiZr has low thermal conductivity because random mass and force-constant fluctuations strongly scatter phonons.
Below the ordered-cluster percolation threshold, HfNbTaTiZr remains in a lower-conductivity disordered-alloy regime.
Formation of large precipitates or secondary phases introduces sufficient scattering to reverse the predicted conductivity increase.
The magnitude of force-constant reduction in B2-like structures in HfNbTaTiZr has not been experimentally verified.
The percolation threshold of HfTi and TiZr clusters in HfNbTaTiZr is unknown.
Broader or unchanged high-frequency linewidths, an unsharpened GVDOS, or lower lattice thermal conductivity in the ordered sample would falsify the proposed reduced-scattering mechanism.
